reader.requirement: An indexed REWRITE must raise invalid key (a) in sequential access when the prime key differs from that of the last record read, (b) in random or dynamic access when no record has that prime key, and (c) in any access mode when a no-duplicates alternate key would equal that of another existing record; the record's own unchanged alternate value and a WITH DUPLICATES key are no conflict.
reader.edition-search: grep of IndexedConnector.cs for DialectBehaviors|Edition: Rewrite consults none (the connector's edition switches cover only READ PREVIOUS after OPEN and the READ duplicate status 02); KeyedIoEmitter passes DialectLevel only at registration
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f16_07 covers one arm; the three lettered conditions in all three access modes and the duplicates-allowed and own-key non-conflicts were probed here

probes.printed: S1 INVALID 21 (sequential, prime changed); S2 INVALID 22 (sequential, alternate collides); S3 OK 02 (duplicates-allowed alternate); R1 INVALID 23 (random, absent); R2 INVALID 22 (random, alternate collides); R3 OK 00 (own alternate); D1 INVALID 23 (dynamic, absent after READ NEXT); D2 INVALID 22; D3 OK 00; record areas unchanged
probes.expected: GR16 a, b and c each raise invalid key (status 21 / 23 / 22); the no-conflict forms succeed

probes.printed: OPEN I-O of an absent indexed file 35, then REWRITE 49 through USE, not INVALID KEY
probes.expected: no invalid key condition on an unopened file

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR16  the text is in the clause or rule: "for which duplicates are not allowed, equals the value of the corresponding data item of a record already existing in the file"

reader.notes: IndexedConnector.Rewrite tests the sequential prime equality (21), the prime's presence (23) and each no-duplicates alternate against the other records (22, itself excluded), all before any change.

refuter.evidence: Probe probes-refute-c07/src/ri2.cob at --std 85 (runs/ri2-002, EXIT 0), dynamic access: after READ of AAA, REWRITE of the existing CCC record (prime differs from the last read) succeeds 00 and replaces CCC (D1 00, D3 CCCC03NEW3), since GR16b tests existence not the last read; a rewrite of BBB whose no-duplicates alternate is changed to CCC's value is invalid 22 and BBB is unchanged (D2 INVALID 22, D4 BBBB02V002); sequential access with prime changed and alternate colliding gives 21 (E1). E2 43 after a failed REWRITE follows IX.4.6.4's successful-READ rule, not this one. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR16 ... is not equal to the value of the prime record key of any record existing in the file'.
